privacy.title: Privacy Policy
sections: Who we are
Angie One is an app by Parra Apps. Contact: angieoneapp.support@gmail.com.
Data on your phone

Your profile (goal, weight, height, age, sex, activity), food diary, water, mood notes, measurements, progress photos and habits are stored only on your device. We have no accounts or servers with your diary.
Photos, voice and text for the AI

If the AI is on, the photo, voice recording or description of your meal (and, for the coach and the plan, the age, weight, goal and preferences you typed in your profile) is sent to our intermediate server (Cloudflare) and to Google Gemini only to answer. We don't keep it. You can turn the AI off in Settings. Progress photos are never sent.
Food database and barcodes

Barcode numbers and searches are checked in our food list (Open Food Facts and USDA). If you add a missing product, we store only the barcode, name, brand and label values, with no personal data, so other people can use it.
Health apps

If you connect Apple Health or Health Connect, Angie One only reads steps, weight and workouts to adjust your daily goal. That data stays on your phone, is never sent to the AI or to third parties, and is never used for ads.
Encrypted cloud backup (optional)
If you turn on the backup, your data is encrypted on your phone with a code only you have. Our server only sees encrypted bytes. You can delete it at any time.
Friends and challenges (optional)
If you join a group, we store your nickname, an anonymous ID and your weekly challenge points. Never your weight, food or health data. You can report and block, and we review every report.
Reports
If you report food data or an AI answer, we store the report text for up to 180 days to fix errors, with no personal data.
We never sell your health data
We don't sell, rent or share your health or food data with advertisers or third parties, and we don't use it for ads. There are no ad trackers.
Your rights and deleting your account

You can delete your account and all your data in Settings → Delete account; this also deletes your cloud backup and takes you out of your friend groups. If you live in California (CCPA), the EU (GDPR) or another place with privacy laws, write to our email to exercise your rights.
Minors
Angie One is not directed at children under 13 (16 in the EU).
Security, breaches and changes

We use encrypted connections (HTTPS). If a breach affects your data we will notify you as the law requires (including the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule). If we change this policy we will show it in the app before it applies.

terms.title: Terms of Use
sections: Acceptance
By using Angie One you accept these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the app.
The service
Angie One helps you log meals and estimate calories with AI. Estimates are approximate and can be wrong.
Trial and subscription

You get 7 days of Premium free with no card. Afterwards you return to the free version; nothing is charged automatically. Then you get a 48-hour offer to lock the price for as long as you stay subscribed. Subscriptions auto-renew and can be cancelled in one tap from your store (App Store or Google Play). The price is shown before you pay.
Acceptable use
Do not use the app for illegal purposes or try to harm it or abuse the AI service.
Not medical advice
Read the Medical disclaimer. The app does not replace a health professional.
Liability
The app is provided "as is". To the extent permitted by law, Parra Apps is not liable for damages arising from the use of estimates.
Contact
Email us at angieoneapp.support@gmail.com.

medical.title: Not medical advice
sections: Not a medical device
Angie One is a general wellness tool. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease.
Estimates
Calories and nutrients calculated by the AI are estimates and may contain significant errors. Review and correct them when needed.
Talk to a professional
Talk to a health professional before making big changes to your diet or exercise, or if you feel pain. If you are under 18, do it with an adult.
Emergencies
If you have a medical emergency, call 911 or your local emergency number.

march.d: Lift your knees one at a time and swing your arms. Go at an easy pace to warm up.

treadmill.d: Walk at a comfortable pace. You should be able to talk while walking.

chairSquat.d: Stand in front of a chair, sit down slowly and stand back up, pushing through your heels.

bridge.d: Lie on your back with knees bent. Lift your hips, squeeze your glutes and lower slowly.

calf.d: Hold a wall or chair. Rise onto your toes and lower slowly.

sideLeg.d: Hold a chair, lift one leg out to the side and lower slowly. Switch legs.

stepUp.d: Step up onto a low, stable step with one foot, then the other, and step down slowly.

legPress.d: Sit on the machine, feet flat on the plate. Push away without locking your knees and return slowly.

gobletSquat.d: Hold a light dumbbell at your chest. Squat down with your back straight and stand up.

wallPush.d: Hands on the wall at chest height. Bend your elbows toward the wall and push back.

armCircles.d: Arms out to the sides, make small circles forward and then backward.

bottleRow.d: Lean forward slightly with a straight back, pull two water bottles toward your waist and lower.

latPull.d: Sit at the machine, pull the bar to your upper chest and let it rise slowly.

seatedRow.d: Sit tall, pull the handle to your belly, squeeze your shoulder blades and return slowly.

chestPress.d: Sit with your back on the pad. Push the handles forward and return slowly.

birdDog.d: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back. Hold, then switch.

deadBug.d: Lie on your back, arms up and knees bent. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg, then switch.

plank.d: On your forearms and toes (or knees), keep your body straight and breathe.

jacks.d: Jump opening legs and arms, then close. For low impact, step out to the side instead.

bike.d: Pedal at a steady pace that makes you breathe a little faster.

stretch.d: Stretch legs, back and arms slowly. Hold each stretch for 15–20 seconds without bouncing.

t6.lNote: Short habit lessons. They are general wellness tips, not medical advice.

plate.1: Fill half your plate with vegetables or fruit.
plate.2: Add a quarter of protein, like eggs, chicken, beans or fish.
plate.3: The last quarter can be rice, arepa, tortilla or potato.

hunger.1: Real hunger grows slowly and any food sounds good.
hunger.2: A craving comes suddenly and asks for something specific.
hunger.3: Wait ten minutes and drink water; then decide calmly.

water.2: Keep a bottle where you can see it.
water.3: A glass with each meal is an easy start.

sleep.1: Sleeping little can increase appetite the next day.
sleep.2: Try going to bed at the same time each night.
sleep.3: Put the phone away thirty minutes before sleeping.

protein.1: Protein helps you feel satisfied for longer.
protein.3: Eggs, yogurt, beans and chicken are simple options.

slip.1: A big meal does not erase your progress.
slip.2: Do not skip the next meal to compensate.
slip.3: Simply return to your usual plan.

move.1: Small walks add up during the day.
move.2: Take the stairs or walk while you talk on the phone.
move.3: Ten minutes after eating feels great.

plan.1: Deciding in advance makes choices easier.
plan.3: Keep healthy snacks ready at home.

ck.guideSub: Weekly plan, progression and tools for your goal.
ck.c4: Move 30 minutes or do your workout
ck.redB: If you have strong pain, chest pain, dizziness, fainting, an injury, pregnancy, an illness, take medication or have a difficult relationship with food, see a doctor, physiotherapist or dietitian. The coach does not diagnose or prescribe.

lose.w1: Week 1: log everything and eat 300 kcal less per day. Walk 20 minutes daily.
lose.w2: Week 2: protein at every meal and 2 full-body strength days.
lose.w3: Week 3: add 1 rep or a little weight per exercise and 2,000 more steps.
lose.w4: Week 4: easy week (fewer sets) and check your average weight, not one day's.

keep.w1: Week 1: eat at your target and note how you feel.
keep.w2: Week 2: 3 strength days and 150 minutes of easy cardio in the week.
keep.w3: Week 3: try 2 new recipes and prep meals for 3 days.
keep.w4: Week 4: easy week and adjust what was hardest.

gain.w1: Week 1: add 300 kcal per day with dense snacks (oats, nuts, smoothies).
gain.w2: Week 2: 3 to 4 strength days with 8 to 12 reps.
gain.w3: Week 3: add a little weight when you complete all sets.
gain.w4: Week 4: easy week and check your weight: aim for 0.25 to 0.5% per week.

nutrition.1: Fill half the plate with vegetables, a quarter protein and a quarter carbs.
nutrition.2: To lose, a 300 to 500 kcal deficit is safe. To gain, 250 to 500 kcal more.

diets.1: The best diet is the one you can keep. Mediterranean has the best evidence.
diets.2: Avoid extreme or 'detox' diets. If you are vegan, you need vitamin B12.

training.1: Strength 2 or 3 days a week and 150 minutes of moderate cardio.
training.2: Progress little by little: 1 more rep or a bit more weight each week.

physio.1: Warm up 5 to 10 minutes and move hips, shoulders and back.
physio.2: If an exercise causes sharp pain, stop and use an easier version.

habits.1: Start with a tiny habit and tie it to something you already do.
habits.2: One bad day doesn't erase your progress: get back on track at the next meal.

sleep.1: Sleep 7 to 9 hours and wake up at the same time every day.
sleep.2: Short sleep increases hunger and cravings.

hydration.1: About 30 to 35 ml per kg a day, more in heat or when training.
hydration.2: A glass of water before meals helps you feel full.

sportsmed.1: Increase volume by at most 10% per week and respect rest days.
sportsmed.2: With chest pain, fainting or swelling, stop and see a doctor.
